projection: South polar stereographic on a 1737.4 km sphere: rho = 2R tan(pi/4 + lat/2), x = rho sin(lon), y = rho cos(lon) (metres, east-positive longitude). Same grid as the NASA PGDA polar products.

terrain.layout: gzip( elevLo[65536] elevHi[65536] slope[65536] ); rows from max y (top) down, columns from min x
terrain.elev: uint16 v: elevation = v/4 - 8000 m (0 = no data); stored as row-wise differences mod 65536, low bytes then high bytes
terrain.slope: uint8 s: slope = s/4 deg (255 = no data); NASA LDSM
terrain.source: NASA LRO LOLA LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ + LDSM_80S_80MPP_ADJ; Barker et al. 2023, PSJ 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole

far.layout: gzip( elevLo elevHi ), same elevation encoding
far.note: LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ block-averaged 4 x 4 (NaN-aware); used for horizon rays beyond 29 km

science.layout: gzip( sun[65536] earth[65536] tavgK[65536] tmaxHalfK[65536] ice2cm[65536] ) uint8 planes

planes.sun: 2 x percent of time the Sun is visible (0-200); 254 = permanently shadowed (NASA LPSR); 255 = no data
planes.earth: 2 x percent of time the Earth is visible (0-200); 255 = no data
planes.tavgK: Diviner annual average temperature (2 cm depth), K; 255 = no data
planes.tmaxHalfK: Diviner annual maximum surface temperature / 2, K; 255 = no data
planes.ice2cm: Diviner depth of stable water ice in 2 cm steps (0-143); 250 = deeper than 2.87 m; 255 = no data

sources: NASA GSFC PGDA AVGVISIB_75S_120M_201608, AVGVISIB_75S_120M_201608_EARTH, LPSR_75S_120M_201608 (hourly over 18.6 years); Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030
NASA LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product dlre_prp_south (PDS Geosciences Node); each 120 m cell takes the PRP triangle that contains its centre

hires.source: NASA GSFC PGDA product 78: LOLA 5 m/pixel south-pole site maps (slope, RMS slope uncertainty, elevation); pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78
hires.layout: h{r}_{c}.bin = gzip(slope5 uint8 deg*4) at 5 m; c{r}_{c}.bin = gzip(slopeErr uint8 deg*20, slope100 uint8 deg*4) at 20 m; 255 = no data
